 PRAYER (in C.M.P.(MD) No.18967 of 2025): Petition filed under Section 1  of the Code of Civil Procedure to grant leave to the petitioner to file  appeal as against the order passed by this Court, dated 04.10.2024 in W  (MD) No.23748 of 2024.

PRAYER (in W.A.(MD) SR No.96251 of 2025): Writ Appeal filed under Claus  15 of Letters Patent to set aside the order passed by this Court, dated  04.10.2024 in W.P.(MD) No.23748 of 2024.
 For Petitioner : Mr.S.Sivakumar  for Mr.Su.Srinivasan
For Respondents : Mr.S.R.A.Ramachandran  Additional Government Pleader   ORDER [Order of the Court was made by DR.G.JAYACHANDRAN, J.]

The land owner, who lost his land for a public purpose, namely. laying of highways road by the National Highways Authority of India,
being aggrieved by the inadequacy of the compensation amount awarded by the acquisition authority by following the old Act i.e., the Land Acquisition Act, _______________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 05/12/2025 04:53:15 pm ) 1894, instead of the new Act, namely the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013),

Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: had filed a writ petition seeking certiorarified mandamus to quash the award passed by the acquisition authority and to refix the compensation amount for his land under the new Act 30 of 2013, which came into force with effect from 01.01.2014.

2. The learned Single Judge, after taking into consideration the provisions of the National Highways The Project Director vs Seshadhri on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184972333/
2 Act, 1956, provisions of the new Act 30 of 2013 as well as the Circular dated 28.12.2017, had remitted the matter back to the Special Tahsildar (Land Acquisition), Madurai-Dhanuskodi,
Paramakudi, to re-work the compensation amount as per the new Act 30 of 2013 and directed to complete the said exercise within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of the order.

entities.text: National Highways The Project Director vs Seshadhri
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said order was passed by the learned Single Judge on 04.10.2024.

3. The Project Director, National Highways Authority of India, who is the requisition authority in the subject matter of land acquisition, is before this Court seeking leave of this Court to prefer a writ appeal as third party as against the order passed by the learned Single Judge, on the ground that the _______________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 05/12/2025 04:53:15 pm )
order passed by the learned Single Judge, without hearing him, has caused prejudice.

The writ petitioner / landlord, who had filed the writ petition, ought to have arrayed the petitioner /
proposed appellant herein being the requisition authority as a party respondent to the writ petition.
However, the writ petitioner failed to do so.
Hence, the impugned order passed by the learned Single Judge requires interference of this Court.

In the grounds of appeal, it is stated that the claim of the writ petitioner to apply the new Act 30 of 2013 is not maintainable, barred by delay, latches, res judicata and contrary to the statutory remedy available under the National Highways Act, 1956.
Some of the judicial pronouncements have also been cited in the grounds of appeal to substantiate the said contentions of the petitioner / proposed appellant.

4. It is to be noted that the land of the writ petitioner was sought to be acquired by issuing a notification, under Section 3A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956, on 18.06.2012 and ultimately,
the same was ended in acquisition and a compensation amount was awarded on 29.12.2014, by following the old Act i.e., the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Having adopted the procedures contemplated under the old Act, the award came to be passed subsequent to the new Act came into effect.

As per the clarification issued by _______________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 05/12/2025 04:53:15 pm ) the Circular dated 28.12.2017, the compensation amount has to be re- determined as per the new Act 30 of 2013.

5. The learned Single Judge, having noted that the Special Tahsildar (Land Acquisition) has not followed the mandatory requirement clarified in the Circular dated 28.12.2017, had remitted matter back to the Special Tahsildar for re-working the compensation amount as per the new Act 30 of 2013.

While ordering so, the learned Single Judge had also taken note of the Judgment passed by the Division Bench of this Court in W.A.(MD) No. 92 of 2022 (The Competent Authority cum District Revenue Officer and others vs. S.Rudhra Devi and another), dated 05.09.2023, wherein, the statutory remedy of preferring appeal before the Arbitrator under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, has been dealt with.

sentences.text: Therefore, the award of the Special Tahsildar (Land Acquisition), without following the mandatory requirement clarified in the Circular dated 28.12.2017 and not following the provisions of the New Act 30 of 2013, has to be necessarily set aside and the matter has to be remitted back to the Special Tahsildar (Land Acquisition) for re-working the compensation amount.

sentences.text: Of course, the writ petitioner has omitted to include the requisition authority, namely, the Project Director, National Highways Authority of India, by not impleading him as a party respondent in the writ petition.

However, the same does not cause prejudice to the Project Director, because in the process of determining the compensation amount, the Special Tahsilar (Land Acquisition) has to necessarily give opportunity to him, if there is any objection or input require to be provided for determination of the compensation amount.

7. Insofar as the delay on the part of the land owner and availability of alternate remedy to him under the statute are concerned, we are of the view that when the constitutional right of the land owner has been deprived by the process established under law, the acquisition authority should follow the procedure established under law scrupulously and there cannot be any deviation.
When there is a gross violation of the procedure established under law, the land owner aggrieved and deprived of his constitutional right can invoke Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
_______________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner / proposed appellant is that the compensation amount was determined on 29.12.2014.

Whereas, the writ petitioner / land owner made a representation to the authority concerned nearly after a lapse of ten years i.e., only on 12.08.2024 and the same was rejected by the acquisition authority on 29.08.2024 and only thereafter, the writ petition was filed.
Thus, the relief sought for in the writ petition suffers from laches.

9. This Court is not oblivious to the fact that the issue regarding application of the new Act 30 of 2013 in respect of the pending acquisition process has been settled by the Honourable Supreme Court as well as by the Circular issued by the concerned Department thereafter and in any case,
where the provisions of the new Act 30 of 2013 have not been applied, the authority concerned should have re-worked the compensation amount and should have paid the fair compensation amount as contemplated under the new Act 30 of 2013, which, in this case, has not been done by the acquisition authority as well as the requisition authority.
This has warranted the erstwhile land owner to make a representation.
At least, at that point of time, the requisition authority as well as the acquisition authority should have _______________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

(
Uploaded on: 05/12/2025 04:53:15 pm ) considered the representation of the land owner and passed appropriate order, which they have not done.

Hence, the writ petition came to be filed by the land owner and the impugned order came to be passed by the learned Single Judge for re-working the compensation amount as per the provisions of the new Act 30 of 2013, as the new Act itself contemplates that compensation for the land acquisition must be fair and adequate.
If the compensation is not calculated as per the new Act 30 of 2013, then the deprivation of the property right, without following the due process of law, will be palpable.

By preferring this civil miscellaneous petition seeking leave of this Court to prefer a writ appeal as third party as against the impugned order passed by the learned Single Judge, will only further delay the process of determining the compensation for the land acquired.

On the contrary, the right of the petitioner herein, namely, requisition authority, the Project Director, National Highways Authority of India, is well protected and no way gets prejudiced by the order of the learned Single Judge.
They can participate in the award proceedings and place the records, as we have stated earlier.

sentences.text: It is also brought to our notice that in an identical case, the Project Director, National Highways Authority of India, was arrayed as one of the respondents and in the said case also, a similar order came to passed by _______________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on:
05/12/2025 04:53:15 pm ) the learned Single Judge directing the authorities concerned to re-work the compensation amount as per the new Act 30 of 2013.

Therefore, granting leave to the petitioner herein and entertaining the writ appeal as third party will only be an empty formality and there will be no change in the order passed by the learned Single Judge.
11. For the foregoing reasons, this civil miscellaneous petition seeking leave of this Court to the petitioner herein to prefer a writ appeal as third party stands dismissed.

Consequently, W.A.(MD)
SR No.96251 of 2025 stands rejected.
